chapter: Shows, scripts and the Mosby-era names
title: Cast and crew of Rhythm Town: Criner, Anderson siblings and student costume makers
summary: Spikes recalls J. Lawrence Criner, Rochester Anderson's sister and brother singing, and USC students who made the costumes.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: On one of these--I can't see where it is now--I saw Effie Smith's name, and uh, then I also saw the name J. Lawrence Criner. Is that...
That's the old actor, Criner.
Yeah. Is that the same Criner that Effie Smith was married to? Effie Smith, the singer?
You mean Effie Smith here?
Yeah.
Well, Lawrence Criner was with the...with the... with Laura Bowman and them in the...in the uh...in the...uh, dramatic world, you know.
That wasn't the same Criner that Effie Smith married?

SPIKES - 184
Reel 5
Page 35
I'm trying to think who Effie Smith was.
She was a singer. She sang and played the piano, and since I ran into both of those names amongst this material somewhere, I wondered...
Effie Smith. I'm trying to think. I can't remember Effie Smith. The name is very familiar.
Okay, you were telling me...

Zelda Jackson...uh, uh, Zelda Anderson was Rochester's sister, and her and her brother did act... This is her brother. We had 'em doin' man 'n' wife, you know, in... Dave Anderson, see. And they sang a song, "On Accounta You," and "You caused me to be so blue you broke my heart..." and so forth. They did that number together, you know, and she was mad at him 'cause he had left her and ever'thing. But they brother and sister.
And "Scenic designs by Joseph L. Hall, Costumes designed by Johnny Jones." Is there anybody else in that cast or in the other credits that is anybody we should know about? Or...

I don't remember these...this is a white boy and girl that made the costumes for... They were students over at U.S.C. And some way they contacted Clarence Muse, and they come over and made all of our costumes for us. They were students over there, you know, and they...they were...oh, this is what I'm talkin' about--Mazie Younkers and Ann Powell--but one of 'em was a boy. They made our costumes for us.
Mmmmm hmmmmm. So Eddie Anderson, who was "Rochester," was in your first show, "Steppin' High," and his children were in...

SPIKES - 185
Reel 5
Page 36
No, not his children. His brother and sister.
Ohhh, I thought you said it was his son. His sister and brother. I see.
Nooo. These were sisters and brothers, too, but they Rochester's sister and brother. She has a nice voice.
I see, his sister and brother were in your show. Did she, uh, sing other places? I mean...I don't remember...
I don't think so. I think she's mostly a church singer. Yeah, she sing in a lot of choirs around here. Never seen her in a cabaret or anything.
